claims.explanation: Vincristine kills cells by stabilizing microtubules and triggering mitotic arrest, and the key determinant of whether arrested cells die is the apoptotic threshold set by MCL1 degradation via FBW7. Loss-of-function FBW7 mutations (seen in NCIH1648, CL11, MKN1) impair MCL1 turnover and should sensitize, while high MCL1 or multidrug transporters (ABCB1/MRP) protect. TP53 pathway status and lineage-specific apoptotic priming modulate the response.

features.basis: FBW7 loss stabilizes MCL1 and impairs its degradation during mitotic arrest, lowering the apoptotic threshold (PMID 21368834); FBXW7-mutant lines (NCIH1648, CL11, MKN1) are among the most killed
MCL1 is the key anti-apoptotic regulator of antitubulin-induced death; high MCL1 protects (PMID 21368834)
P-glycoprotein efflux of vincristine confers resistance (PMID 7214365)
MRP overexpression confers moderate vincristine resistance (PMID 7954421)
TP53-mutant lines dominate the most-killed set, consistent with impaired DNA-damage/apoptotic checkpoints after mitotic arrest
PTEN loss (ZR751, UACC62, HEC265) increases PI3K/AKT-dependent mitotic vulnerability
BRAF-mutant melanomas (IGR37, K029AX, UACC62) are enriched among killed lines, possibly via MAPK-driven mitotic priming
NRAS-mutant lines (IPC298, KU1919) appear in the sensitive set
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1437) are among the least affected
SARM1 NADase mediates vincristine-induced axonal degeneration; low SARM1 may reduce drug toxicity (PMID 28334607)
